title: Derived relative cup products commute with base change of ringed spaces
statement:
Let $X,X',Y,Y'$ be topological spaces equipped with sheaves of commutative rings, with all open-set sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ be morphisms of ringed spaces with $fg'=gf'$, including equality of the ring-sheaf maps. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived direct images computed by K-injectives [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and $Lv^*$ computed by taking a K-flat resolution before applying $v^*M=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{source}}\otimes_{v^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathrm{target}}}v^{-1}M$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use the canonical derived pullback-direct-image adjunctions [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general]. For $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ let $c_f:Rf_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*L\to Rf_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)$ be the relative cup product: its transpose is the pullback tensor comparison followed by the tensor of the two counits [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. Define $\beta_M:Lg^*Rf_*M\to Rf'_*Lg'^*M$ as the adjunct of
$$Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*M\simeq Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*M\xrightarrow{Lg'^*\varepsilon_M}Lg'^*M.$$
For every $K,L$, the following two morphisms from $Lg^*(Rf_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*L)$ to $Rf'_*(Lg'^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg'^*L)$ are equal in $D(\mathcal O_{Y'})$:
$$Rf'_*(\mu_{g'})\circ\beta_{K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L}\circ Lg^*(c_f)
=c_{f'}\circ(\beta_K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\beta_L)\circ\mu_g,$$
where $\mu_v:Lv^*(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)\simeq Lv^*P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lv^*Q$ is the canonical tensor comparison. The equality is natural in both complexes, so it remains valid after a coefficient morphism $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ and its pullback are composed with the two sides. No Cartesian, flatness, quasi-coherence, boundedness or invertibility assumption on $\beta$ is required.

proof.text:
Write $F=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $B=Lg^*$, $H=Lg'^*$, $C=Lf'^*$ and $S=Rf'_*$. Write $t_V$ for the tensor comparison of a pullback $V$, and $\theta:CB\cong HF$ for the canonical square comparison. All tensors below are derived, and juxtaposition of maps means composition from right to left. Apply the ringed-topos projection/exchange statement to the given square of ringed spaces, using their open-set sites. Its hypotheses are precisely small sites, commutation of the square including ring maps, and the canonical derived adjunctions; its exchange map is our $\beta$, since both transpose to $H(\varepsilon_M)\theta_{RM}$. Let $\pi_{K,Q}:RK\otimes Q\to R(K\otimes FQ)$ and $\pi'$ denote its projection maps. The theorem gives, for every $Q\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$,
$$S(t_H)\beta_{K\otimes FQ}B(\pi_{K,Q})=S(1_{HK}\otimes\theta_Q)\pi'_{HK,BQ}(\beta_K\otimes1_{BQ})t_B.$$
This orientation follows by composing the theorem's target identification $1\otimes\theta_Q^{-1}$ with $1\otimes\theta_Q$. No inverse to $\pi$ or $\beta$ is used.

proof.text:
The relative cup product factors as
$$c_{f,K,L}=R(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)\pi_{K,RL}.$$
Indeed the transpose of the right side under $F\dashv R$ is $(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)(\varepsilon_K\otimes1_{FRL})t_F=(\varepsilon_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)t_F$, exactly the defining transpose of the relative cup product. The natural Hom-bijection is injective, proving the factorization. The identical argument gives $c_{f',HK,HL}=S(1_{HK}\otimes\varepsilon'_{HL})\pi'_{HK,SHL}$. This uses only the stated definition of each projection map and the cup definition, not any projection-formula isomorphism.

proof.text:
Put $Q=RL$ in Step 1 and postcompose with $S(1_{HK}\otimes H\varepsilon_L)$. Naturality of $\beta$ for $1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L:K\otimes FRL\to K\otimes L$, and naturality of $t_H$, identify its left side with $S(t_H)\beta_{K\otimes L}B(c_{f,K,L})$, by Step 2. Thus this side of the desired identity equals
$$S(1_{HK}\otimes(H\varepsilon_L\circ\theta_{RL}))\pi'_{HK,BRL}(\beta_K\otimes1_{BRL})t_B.$$
The two naturality substitutions here are $\beta_{K\otimes L}BR(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)=SH(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)\beta_{K\otimes FRL}$ and $t_H H(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)=(1\otimes H\varepsilon_L)t_H$.

proof.text:
The defining mate equation is
$$H\varepsilon_L\circ\theta_{RL}=\varepsilon'_{HL}\circ C(\beta_L).$$
It follows either from the transpose characterization of mates or directly by expanding the adjunct and cancelling $\varepsilon'_{CA}C\eta'_A=1_{CA}$. Replace the parenthesized factor of Step 3 by this expression. Naturality of $\pi'$ in its second variable for $\beta_L:BRL\to SHL$ gives
$$S(1_{HK}\otimes C\beta_L)\pi'_{HK,BRL}=\pi'_{HK,SHL}(1_{SHK}\otimes\beta_L).$$
Consequently Step 3 becomes $S(1_{HK}\otimes\varepsilon'_{HL})\pi'_{HK,SHL}(\beta_K\otimes\beta_L)t_B$. Step 2 identifies this with $c_{f',HK,HL}(\beta_K\otimes\beta_L)t_B$, the required right side.

proof.text: Every comparison and counit used above is natural, the projection maps are natural in both arguments, and the adjunction Hom-bijections are bifunctorial. Hence the equality is natural in $K,L$. For a coefficient morphism $a:K\otimes L\to M$, the naturality equation $\beta_M BR(a)=SH(a)\beta_{K\otimes L}$ identifies the coefficient-composed first route, followed by $SH(a)S(t_H)^{-1}$, with $\beta_M B(R(a)c_f)$. Postcomposing the established equality with that same map proves the coefficient-valued compatibility. No condition on the square beyond ringed commutation entered: arbitrary unbounded complexes, nonflat coefficient maps and noninvertible exchange maps are included.
